evals.prompt: Write a Python function that calculates the total price for a shopping cart. Requirements: takes a list of items (each with price and quantity), applies a tax rate (default 19%), if total before tax exceeds 100 EUR apply a 10% discount before tax, if express shipping is selected add a flat fee of 5.99 EUR, return final total rounded to 2 decimals.
evals.expected_output: Clean code written from scratch — no dirty-then-fix pattern. Names are descriptive, constants are named, conditionals are simple, units are in names where applicable.
expectations: Function and parameter names are descriptive from the start (N1) — no single-letter variables like t, s, x
Monetary constants are named: TAX_RATE, DISCOUNT_RATE, DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD, EXPRESS_SHIPPING_FEE or similar (G25)
Variables with units include the unit in the name where ambiguous, e.g. discount_threshold_eur or shipping_fee_eur (N4)
Each if-condition tests only one thing (G28) — no compound boolean expressions inline
Conditions are in positive form (G29) — no double negatives
Function does one thing or is clearly decomposed (G30)
No magic numbers appear in the function body (G25)
No boolean flag arguments like is_express (F3) — use separate functions instead
Functions have 0–2 arguments (F1) — 3+ arguments must be justified or restructured
Code does NOT show a pattern of writing dirty code then flagging it for cleanup — it should be clean on first write
Findings section is either empty or contains only minor [ ] flags — not a long list of self-inflicted violations
